name: Ishbilia
reason: Family-run off William Street since 1998; the charcoal grill's smoke reaches Harrods shoppers before the menu does.

name: The Mantl
reason: Charcoal-grilled Turkish directly opposite Harrods; the 220-day dry-aged Iskender is why it out-books its neighbours.

name: Chisou
reason: No scene, no sushi-for-Instagram lighting — just a two-decade-old counter doing proper nigiri two minutes off Beauchamp Place.

name: Andipa Gallery
reason: Same Knightsbridge townhouse since 1967, and still the first call in London for a serious Banksy or Pop Art acquisition.

name: Harrods Food Halls
reason: Live music some evenings under the original tiled ceiling, and a rotisserie-chicken queue that never quite dies down.

name: Medlar
reason: Michelin Bib Gourmand held since 2025 and retained for 2026 — precise, unfussy French-inflected cooking on the quiet World's End stretch of King's Road.

name: Martino's
reason: Grace Dent's 'beautiful bedlam' verdict stuck — a glossy 1950s-trattoria reboot on Sloane Square's corner that turns ordinary diners into film extras for the night.

name: The March Hare
reason: Alice-in-Wonderland cocktail pedigree from Shoreditch's Callooh Callay, with a bottle of Champagne and £2 oysters running most weekend afternoons.

name: The Wee Sister
reason: An Irish-leaning wine list and a properly poured Guinness next door to sister restaurant Myrtle — regulars get their pint started before they've ordered.

name: Saatchi Gallery
reason: Nine exhibition spaces and free entry on Duke of York Square, with the hang turning over often enough to be worth a second visit.

name: Chelsea Physic Garden
reason: Four walled acres since 1673, the country's largest olive tree included — arrive at opening to have the paths to yourself before the crowds.

name: Kitty Fisher's
reason: A Georgian townhouse in Shepherd Market that's been full since 2014; the menu gets rewritten around the season, never around a concept.

name: Bellamy's
reason: Same chef, same manager, twenty years running — a Franco-Belgian oyster bar tucked into a mews that regulars still call a club with no sub.

name: 5 Hertford Street
reason: Invitation only, proposer and seconder required — the front door everyone talks about leads down to Loulou's, a basement nightclub that never quite goes out of fashion.

name: Hedonism Wines
reason: Six thousand-odd bottles and a basement built around a vertical of Yquem — pull up to the tasting wall and try a first-growth by the glass, no case required.

name: Connaught Brown
reason: Impressionist and Modern masters shown three or four times a year in a single Albemarle Street room that hasn't needed a second location since 1985.

name: Salloos
reason: Family-run since 1976, and the tandoori lamb chops — cooked over charcoal in the same kitchen for half a century — are still what regulars book the table for.

name: The Nag's Head
reason: No phones, no children, no small talk — the same house rules the publican's kept since 1982, pewter mugs and all.

name: Rose Uniacke
reason: Three shopfronts along one stretch of Pimlico Road, all hers — Georgian oak sits next to 1970s Italian glass, and nothing is labelled cheap.

name: Mungo & Maud
reason: Leather dog beds and hand-stitched collars for a clientele who take their pets as seriously as their tailoring.

name: La Poule au Pot
reason: Candlelit even at lunch, with a terrace that fills first — the cassoulet has barely changed since the Frankels opened it more than fifty years ago.

name: Peggy Porschen
reason: The pink façade draws the queue, but everything's baked in-house every morning — this is the original, not a copy of one.

name: Core by Clare Smyth
reason: Three Michelin stars in a Notting Hill townhouse, and the tasting menu still opens with a potato that tastes like nothing else in London.

name: Julie's Restaurant
reason: A 1969 Notting Hill fixture, closed and reborn in 2024 under a longtime regular turned owner, with a champagne bar built into the name.

name: Sova
reason: Low-intervention Georgian and Ukrainian wines poured over vinyl and guest DJs, in the old Zima space on Blenheim Crescent.

name: Themes and Variations
reason: London's first design-only gallery, run by the same owner since 1984 — still the UK's exclusive agent for Fornasetti.

name: The Notting Hill Bookshop
reason: The real shop behind the 1999 film, run independently by two brothers since the chain that briefly owned it collapsed.

name: Books for Cooks
reason: Cookbooks on the shelves and today's recipe pulled straight from one of them, served at the lunch counter — the test kitchen's run this way since 1983.

name: Wiltons
reason: Oysters and Dover sole in a room the same family has owned since 1942; nothing on the menu has chased a trend since.

name: Franco's
reason: London's oldest Italian dining room, on Jermyn Street since 1946, still pulling espresso at breakfast through to the last dinner cover.

name: Chris Beetles Gallery
reason: Forty years dealing in British illustration and watercolours on Ryder Street, with the hang turning over most months.

name: Spencer House
reason: Diana's family seat before the Palace years — Palladian state rooms original, not restored-to-look-like, and open to the public one day a week only.

name: The Globe
reason: Three storeys up inside Al Faisaliah's golden sphere, with the whole of King Fahd Road laid out below by sunset.

name: Bossco Roastery
reason: A roastery-first counter on Olaya Street running the full spectrum from V60 to Spanish latte, Kingdom Tower framed in the window.

name: Poloné
reason: An outdoor terrace off Musa Ibn Nusair Street that's as much about the shisha as the lattes, and doesn't quiet down before 1am.

name: Chèrie
reason: Industrial concrete and soft light, a second-floor window framing Al Faisaliah Tower — tiramisu and Spanish lattes both doing the heavy lifting.

name: Ahlam Gallery
reason: One of Al Mousa Centre's largest rooms, founded by a doctor turned gallerist; recent shows have run to AI-and-robotics canvases during Art Week Riyadh.

name: Kuro Cafe
reason: Hand-whipped soufflé pancakes take twenty minutes to arrive; the coconut matcha doesn't make you wait.

name: The Vinyl Ember
reason: Vinyl spins and the open fire stays lit down in KAFD's sunken Wadi level, the mocktail list turning bolder as the night deepens.

name: TAKYA
reason: Three founders spent years chasing regional recipes across the Kingdom; the plating is modern, but the flavours are someone's actual grandmother's.

name: Altopiano
reason: Homegrown, but the risotto and the tasting menu don't know it — dates just quietly turn up in the burrata.

name: Aseeb
reason: A husband and wife cook Najd's home food the way their own mothers did — palm fronds go in the fire, not just the décor.

name: Base & Boon
reason: Two Saudi cousins turned a manicure bar into a design object; the Zallal outpost pairs nail art with its own café, and none of the usual mall-salon flatness.

name: SAMOCA
reason: Saudi Arabia's first contemporary art museum, built into a warehouse shell that still remembers what it used to hold.

name: Athr JAX
reason: Jeddah's most serious gallery brought its programme north into a JAX warehouse, and the artists it shows haven't softened for the new postcode.

name: Hafez Gallery
reason: A Jeddah gallery's second act, betting Riyadh's newest art crowd will follow Saudi and Arab painters north to a warehouse floor.

name: Lift
reason: A princess's project space turned institution — exhibitions, a co-working floor and a concept shop under one warehouse roof, with a programme that doesn't play it safe.

name: Origin Café & Roasters
reason: Tiered cement counters under a skylight, the roasting kit in full view of the cupping bar — a warehouse converted for people who take the bean seriously.

name: Robata
reason: A robata grill run by the same chefs behind Myazu, one of MENA's 50 Best — smoke, skewers, and a Hittin address with no international name over the door.

name: Hewar Art Gallery
reason: Fifty-two floors above Olaya inside Kingdom Tower, championing Saudi and Arab contemporary art since 2005 — dialogue over decoration, true to its Arabic name.

name: Lyrs Artisan Bakery
reason: Newly landed in Akariya Plaza with a laminated Japanese-toast obsession that already has Olaya queuing before breakfast.

name: HODAJ
reason: A single Najdi mud-brick room turned coffee-and-matcha bar, shelved with hand-picked ceramics — it reads more concept store than café.

name: Ghaymat Samhan
reason: Soft-serve done small and seasonal — a two-person operation still finding its feet, which is exactly why it's worth catching before everyone else does.

name: Saba Lounge
reason: A rooftop lounge that actually earns its At-Turaif view — the closest thing this district has to a proper evening hangout.

name: OffBrief
reason: Art deco angles inside a raw warehouse shell, a menu split into Hot, Cold, Not Coffee and Hungry that refuses to take itself seriously while the espresso does.

name: With Heart
reason: A coffee counter dropped into a working gallery, pulling shots between print racks with photography and workshop sessions running alongside.

name: Personage
reason: Racks of homegrown labels sit beside international streetwear, with a live screen-printing station turning the shop floor into a working studio during exhibitions.

name: Kasbah
reason: Marrakech-red interiors and a tea ceremony performed table-side, poured from height without a drop spilled — Boulevard City's most theatrical import.

name: Fire Station Social Cucina
reason: Took over the old Gusto site on London Road and turned it into a pizza theatre built around a wood oven. Hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and barely any local competition doing it this way.
